items.title: Read recent ordinary-session history directly from Hermes Agent
items.body:
## Parent and prerequisite

Child of #43. Builds on the independently configured Agent hosts in #44. #44 must land before this child can merge; local work can be stacked without changing the maintainer’s master checkout.

## Outcome

From the direct Agent session list, open an ordinary session and read a bounded recent-history preview without resuming a runtime, sending a message, or requiring WebUI. This is the next slice toward a working direct-Agent conversation.

## Scope and verified starting contract

Use the Agent's authenticated REST session-detail and message endpoints, with explicit Profile routing and the same per-host cookie/auth ownership as the connection handshake. Source inspected in installed ARC Agent `5742b5ec1d9d4e10763eea22570b912d219ca6ad`, `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py::get_session_detail` and `get_session_messages`. Refresh against the selected runtime/current upstream at implementation time.

- `GET /api/sessions/{exact-session-id}?profile=<profile>` returns the selected session’s metadata and serving Profile.
- `GET /api/sessions/{exact-session-id}/messages?profile=<profile>&limit=100&offset=0&order=latest&inline_images=false` returns a bounded, projected recent-history window, canonical resolved `session_id`, serving `profile`, and `pagination` metadata. Compression ancestors are resolved by the server.
- Preserve the selected durable identity and the server’s resolved continuation separately; reject a wrong host/Profile/session response. Do not assume the Bot Chat canonical-session rules apply to ordinary sessions.
- Render server-projected text, user/assistant/tool/system roles and available display markers tolerantly, with stable row identity. Preserve unknown/optional fields without crashing. Display attachment placeholders honestly; file download/preview is a later concern.
- Show that this is a read-only recent window, with refresh and explicit unavailable/empty states. Do not claim the full transcript is loaded or invent an older-page cursor. The server reports projected row counts, which can differ from raw pagination counts; robust older-history navigation is a later contract-bound slice.
- Cancel when leaving the view or switching host/Profile; late responses cannot replace the current view’s history. No offline cache in this slice.

## Exclusions

No `session.resume`, session creation/send, runtime ownership, approval handling, data migration, WebUI sidecar reads, file download, offline caching, Android changes, or new dependency. No direct access to Agent storage from the phone. No new backend endpoint.

## Acceptance and validation

- Read an existing ordinary session from the Agent list and refresh its recent projected history.
- Test exact endpoint/query encoding, bounds, tolerant projected-message decoding, stable row identity, host/Profile/canonical identity checks, auth/missing-session failures, cancellation and stale responses with URLProtocol/scripted fixtures.
- Verify the wire shape on an in-scope authenticated live host without session mutations; output only aggregate evidence, never transcripts or credentials.
- Run focused XCTest and `scripts/validate`, then one signed Debug simulator pass and a concise manual plan for two hosts/Profiles, compression lineage, light/dark, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver.

## Risk, rollback and ownership

Read-only HTTP access must not create or resume a runtime. If history is unsupported or identity cannot be established, show an explicit failure rather than another conversation’s data. Removing the preview changes no server-side state. Main app/test membership only in this slice; share/widget/system routing remains tracked in #43.

ACH9001 implements in a temporary issue-bound worktree and records the agent engine in the commit trailer. martinezhermes owns product decisions and independent review. Git push, PR publication/merge and TestFlight upload require separate explicit maintainer instruction.

items.title: [COMPUTER USE] Whole-computer agent and harness distillation into Hermes: done, missing, acceptance checks
items.body:
# Computer use: whole-computer agent and harness distillation into Hermes

This is a standalone issue for computer use only. It states what is done, what is missing, and every route for distilling a reference assistant's behavior into the Hermes agent inside Dani-Dex.

Scope: **computer use only**. Goal: a generalized agent that can use the whole computer, and a distillation program that moves a reference assistant's observable behavior into the Hermes agent running inside Dani-Dex. Behavior terms only: what the agent does and how to verify it. No secrets.

All commits are authored and committed as Somdipto Nandy <somdiptonandy@gmail.com>, local only, not pushed (needs the owner's go). Test today from the Drive bundle `dani-alexa-ram.bundle`, file id `1J0oUFc__cUGJYb-nQ8X50YB6nR11Kz-N` (folder `1njdaA-5Hox4LKoKNnZrYH_QxRvvQ8V4R`). `git clone dani-alexa-ram.bundle dani-alexa`; install the Dani-Dex runtime per the repo README; then `scripts/desktop-up.sh`.

Reading of the names, from public pages, please confirm: "Hermes" = Hermes Agent by Nous Research (MIT, https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent, docs https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/). It is not in this repo; today's harness is a different executor. Everything below that says "Hermes" needs the owner's yes on that reading.

---
### PART A - DONE (computer-use only), with how to verify

| # | Capability | Commit | Verify |
|---|-----------|--------|--------|
| A1 | Screen read: accessibility tree of any native window (needs session bus, accessibility bus, window manager; all set up by one script) | 580c83e | `scripts/desktop-up.sh && node --test test/desktop-control.regression.mjs` check 1 |
| A2 | Mouse and keyboard by element token, not pixels | 580c83e | same file, check 2 (types into a field, reads the value back) |
| A3 | App launch from an allowlist, window found within 10 s, window can be closed | 580c83e | check 3 |
| A4 | Window list and focus by title | 580c83e | check 5 |
| A5 | Native file dialog: typed a path into a real file chooser, got the file back | 580c83e | check 4 |
| A6 | Recovery: a second identical desktop failure returns the window list and next steps instead of looping | 3749d62 | check 6 |
| A7 | Driver refusals count as failures (they used to return as success text) | 3749d62 | check 6 |
| A8 | 60 s overall deadline on every browser call (one call hung 250 s) | 305fb97 | `node --test test/site-memory.test.js`, deadline check |
| A9 | Tool guidance is labelled as tool guidance so the agent cannot quote it as page content | 956b053 | same file |
| A10 | Per-site memory: host-keyed hints from `docs/site-memory.json` injected into page reads | 381531d | same file |
| A11 | Web UI primitives: re-open guard, repeat-call breaker, custom dropdown select, date inputs, embedded-frame hint, plain "I am not a robot" checkbox by real click (a puzzle means stop and report), idle-browser reaper, heavy-resource blocking | 2b40ca4 .. 93a706e | `node --test test/computer-use.regression.mjs` (7 checks, about 40 s) |
| A12 | Completion-proof gate: a task finishes "done" only with exact on-screen confirmation text or an id; a blocker becomes "blocked", never "done" | e7a3b1e | `node --test test/receipts-approvals.test.js` |
| A13 | Approval gate library: action bound to exact recipient and words, owner-only grants | e7a3b1e | same file (not yet wired to a send path) |
| A14 | Distillation scoreboard and behavior spec: one row per target behavior with its check; 4 of 10 have a check today, 6 pending | latest | `node scripts/scoreboard.mjs --fast` |
| A15 | Lessons log, 24 entries, each names the flaw, the fix and the check | docs/computer-use-lessons.md | read it |

Unit total: `node --test test/receipts-approvals.test.js test/gateway.test.js test/mcp.test.js test/site-memory.test.js` = 32 pass, 0 fail (2026-10-22 22:38). Desktop regression 6/6 (22:25).

---
### PART B - HARNESS DISTILLATION: every way to do it, with state and acceptance check

Definition: distillation = take the reference assistant's observable behavior (what it does at each step of a computer task) and make the Hermes agent inside Dani-Dex reproduce it, measurably, at zero incremental cost. Each route below is independent; the final system uses several. A behavior is "distilled" only when its check passes on the Hermes agent, not when the code merely exists.

**Behaviors to distill (the target spec, in plain terms)**
1. Check live state before acting; never rely on remembered state.
2. After every step, confirm the screen changed as intended; on a mismatch, stop and re-read.
3. Count a task done only on visible proof.
4. Switch strategy after two failed tries; never repeat the same failing call.
5. Stop at obstacles that need a human (challenge puzzles, sensitive fields, missing permission) and report them plainly.
6. Show exact words and recipient before anything is sent as the owner.
7. Ask the owner only for gaps that change the outcome; otherwise fill from context.
8. Keep secrets out of text; secrets only through a vault.
9. Keep follow-up wakes; report short and only what changed.
10. Recover from stuck states (stray dialogs, wrong window, hung page) without the owner.

**Distillation routes**

| # | Route | What it does | State | Acceptance check |
|---|-------|--------------|-------|------------------|
| D1 | Behavior spec to checklist | Turn behaviors 1-10 into numbered, testable statements, each with a pass/fail scenario | Started: `docs/behavior-spec.json` lists B1-B10; 6 have no scenario yet | 10 scenarios exist as scripts; a human can read each in under a minute |
| D2 | Gate distillation (code, not prompt) | Move rules into code that cannot be talked around: completion proof, approval binding, stop-at-obstacle, secret handling | Partial: A12, A13 done; obstacle and sensitive-field gates not built | Each gate has a negative test where the agent tries to bypass it and is refused |
| D3 | Tool-contract distillation | Shape tool names, descriptions and error texts so the agent is steered to the right next call (hint labelling, recovery notes) | Partial: A6, A9, A10 | For each failure seen, the error text names the next call; replay shows the agent takes it |
| D4 | Skill distillation | Save a successful run as a reusable skill with its own success check; replay it | Not started. Hermes has a skills system to host this | Replay of a saved skill ends with the same proof in fewer calls |
| D5 | Memory distillation | Per-site and per-app facts learned from failures, recalled automatically | Partial: A10 (static file) | A fact added after a failure is injected on the next visit; remove it and the failure returns |
| D6 | Trace distillation | Record step-by-step runs of the reference behavior on fixed tasks, then compare the Hermes agent's steps against them | Not started | Same 10 tasks, per-step diff report; target at least 90 percent of steps equivalent |
| D7 | Eval-driven distillation | Every failure becomes a regression check before the fix ships | Done as practice (24 lessons, 3 regression files) | No lesson without a check; CI runs all files |
| D8 | Teacher-student A/B | Run the same tasks through the current executor and Hermes on the same VM and free inference; keep the better one per behavior | Not started. Needs the owner's yes on the Hermes reading and a VM | Scorecard per behavior: proof rate, calls per task, false completions, stalls, RAM peak |
| D9 | Judge distillation | A cheap local checker scores each run against behaviors 1-10 from the logs | Not started | Judge agrees with a human on 20 labelled runs at 90 percent or more |
| D10 | Recovery-policy distillation | Encode recovery steps per stuck type (stray dialog, wrong window, hung page, dead session) | Partial: A6 and A8 | Fault-injection test per type; agent recovers with no human input |
| D11 | Prompt/policy distillation | The short instruction text the agent sees, kept minimal and generated from D1 | Partial (hand-written) | Prompt is generated from the spec file; changing the spec changes behavior in a check |
| D12 | Inference-route resilience | Probe free routes, switch when one hits a limit, never pay | Not started (manual so far) | Simulated limit message: switch within 60 s |
| D13 | Distillation scoreboard | One file listing each behavior, its check, current pass/fail on the Hermes agent | Built (`scripts/scoreboard.mjs`); runs against the current executor, not yet against Hermes | `node scripts/scoreboard.mjs` prints 10 rows; CI fails on regression |

**Order of work**: finish D1, then D2, D3, D7 (continuous), D5, D10, D8 once the owner confirms Hermes and a VM exists, then D6, D9, D4, D11, D12.

---
### PART C - PENDING COMPUTER-USE ITEMS (not done)

| # | Item | State | Acceptance check |
|---|------|-------|------------------|
| C1 | Visual verify after each step | Missing. Agents read text and element trees, never pixels | Screenshot at completion and on stall plus a local check; a deliberately broken step is caught by the pixel check |
| C2 | Screenshot proof saved with every completion | Missing | Every "done" carries a PNG path |
| C3 | Sensitive-field stop rule in code (payment, credentials not from the vault) | Prompt rule only | Local test page with a card field: agent returns "blocked", never fills |
| C4 | Session persistence | Partial; a sandbox wipe loses state (about 10 so far) | Kill everything, restore from an encrypted export, still signed in |
| C5 | Control of the owner's real machine | Virtual desktop works; real machine needs a bridge process | The 6 desktop checks pass against the real machine |
| C6 | Parallel stability | One agent stable; two thrash on 2 GB | 3 agents, load under 4 for 30 min on a 4 GB or larger VM |
| C7 | Idle-session watchdog and re-nudge gap | Open. Stalls sometimes last minutes before a re-prompt | An idle busy session is aborted and re-prompted within 130 s, 20 runs |
| C8 | Mail and verification-code reading without a browser | Not built. Needs the owner to enable IMAP and save an app password through a vault link | Read-only module (no write verbs); a code mail is fetched |
| C9 | Outbound-as-owner send path using the approval gate | Not built | A send without exact recipient and words approval is refused |
| C10 | Push to a branch | Blocked on the owner's go | One change per PR, with video, branch `prod-2` only |

### Needed from the owner
1. Yes or no: is "Hermes" = Hermes Agent (Nous Research)? If not, the name or link.
2. A 4 GB or larger VM (C6, D8).
3. Go for a branch push (C10).
4. IMAP app password via a vault link (C8), and a route to the real machine (C5) or a decision to skip.

items.title: [RESEARCH ONLY] Evaluate Hermes Agent as bundled Windows AI research backend for ETF AI Cockpit
items.body:
> **Status: OPEN — RESEARCH / DISCOVERY ONLY (19 October 2026).** This is an **unmanaged GitHub research issue**, created at the owner's request. It is **not** a canonical `ISSUE-xxxx`, implementation acceptance, permission to install or enable an agent, dependency change, programme-state transition, or authority to operate markets. Admission of any later product work must go through the reviewed Codex-root control plane and exact-head gates.

## Objective

Determine whether **[Nous Research Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)** is worth incorporating **inside the installed ETF AI Cockpit Windows application** as a locally managed, optional, autonomous AI research backend. The intended user experience is **one installer / one ETF AI Cockpit UI**, with no separate Hermes interface or manual Hermes install for the end user if bundled.

Evaluate commercial/redistribution feasibility, real runtime isolation, costs, feature value, security and **whether it provides advantages over the existing Python/Flet, scheduler, typed application API, provider pipeline and optional local-LLM commentary**. **Do not implement or deploy in this issue.**

### Why this matters — discussion summary

Owner asks:
1. Can Hermes run as part of the backend after someone downloads and installs an ETF AI Cockpit `.exe`? **Yes in principle:** Hermes exposes programmatic ACP, TUI gateway JSON-RPC and an OpenAI-compatible HTTP/SSE server. Windows-native execution is documented, but **a turnkey bundled ETF installer is not provided**; the compatibility, dependencies and lifecycle are a custom integration task.
2. Can it become the research AI for stock picking, financial documents, forecasts and app operation? **Potentially:** perform source-grounded annual-report/earnings research, scheduled watchlist and data-quality monitoring, company comparisons, agent skills/memory and delegated evidence gathering. **It is not a validated stock-return predictor** and does not replace TimesFM/Toto, canonical scoring or deterministic gates.
3. Can it run unattended? **Only while its gateway/backend remains running**, and with explicit background-service/autorun consent. No silent network activity or background installation.

Full prior discussion, source research and integration analysis (access-controlled): [19 Oct 2026 research archive](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bY95HwvYub35bof37qOcqBqk40ZAR8toGhN08RcwdXs/edit).

## Verified app starting point (GitHub main checked 19 Oct 2026)

- Repository `README.md`: Python/Flet, Windows-first, usually browser UI on `127.0.0.1:8550`; Flet one-folder/portable packaging via `scripts/build_windows.bat`. Forecasts via separate TimesFM/Toto adapters; model weights kept outside the packaged executable.
- `pyproject.toml`: base Python `>=3.11`; optional AI model dependencies; bundling another rapidly evolving Python/Node stack can cause dependency conflicts.
- `configs/local_llm.yaml`: existing optional local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (default `http://localhost:1234/v1`) provides constrained explanatory/audit commentary rather than authoritative financial calculations.
- `src/etf_cockpit/signals/canonical_scoring.py` distinguishes research attractiveness, expected returns, risk and evidence confidence; `src/etf_cockpit/models/forecast_scores.py` binds forecasts to data/provenance.
- `AGENTS.md`, `docs/development/CONTROL_PLANE.md`: **local-first; `execution_allowed=false`; no live orders, broker/provider writes, silent cloud uploads, privileged programme/GitHub changes, invented data, zero-fill or point-in-time leakage**.

## Research tracks

### A. Windows EXE / installer and API embedding
Compare with a decision matrix:
- **Preferred hypothesis: bundled independent Hermes sidecar** with separately pinned Python/Node/runtime and user-data directory, managed process startup/health/shutdown, local API, model configuration, limited permissions and optional background mode.
- Installer-triggered, **consented** first-run Hermes setup (smaller download, but requires internet and verified supply chain).
- Same-process Python import (likely harder to isolate failures/dependencies).
- Remote gateway/service (different privacy/cost/availability trade-off; not preferred for local-first operation).

Verify *actual* Windows 10 and 11 paths, signed MSIX vs bootstrap installer distinctions, Flet one-folder portability, Python 3.14 Hermes runtime versus app's current Python/model stack, size (MB), installation/first-run/offline/uninstall/update/rollback behaviour, executable signing and per-user writable storage. Check all dependency licences and redistribution; Hermes core advertises MIT, but transitive licences/weights/tools must be audited.

API candidates: **HTTP + SSE**, **JSON-RPC stdio/WebSocket**, **ACP**. Test streaming, cancellation, approvals, persistent sessions, structured results, local-only binding and secure per-install authentication. No bearer key in web-rendered Flet UI, logs or bundle. Prevent inadvertently exposing unrestricted terminal/filesystem/network functions through the API.

### B. End-user research capabilities
Investigate realistic read-only operations:
- Annual/quarterly reports: source-cited cash flow, margins, debt, dilution, guidance, peers and valuation assumptions, labelled dates/currencies/units.
- Research dossiers for stocks, ETFs and Norwegian savings banks; bull/base/bear analysis with explicit uncertainty and missing/conflicting states.
- Controlled nightly/watchlist earnings and changes research, earnings or provider anomaly alerts, scheduled analysis and local reports; compare to simple deterministic Python jobs first.
- Multi-model routing to local llama.cpp/LM Studio/Ollama or authorised cloud APIs; no bundled model intelligence or guaranteed free calls. Measure user-level costs, speed, RAM/VRAM and offline behaviour.
- Skills, curated memory, scheduled jobs, subagents, longitudinal research and controlled optional notifications. Define source versioning, retention, user opt-in, export and deletion.
- Read-only developer aide: GitHub/CI/V8-bughunt status reports, **not** commits, merges, PR/lifecycle writes or self-approved code fixes.

### C. Security and product architecture
Propose a minimal typed, allowlisted **research facade** over existing validated Cockpit application APIs. Hermes does **not** gain direct access to canonical financial calculations, the database write path, broker keys, the release/control plane, privileged shell commands, or unrestricted filesystem/network by default.

Threat-model prompt injection from issuers/websites, tool escalation, malicious skills/MCP servers, local API access, secret exfiltration, stale data, replay/memory contamination, hallucination, automatic background service, telemetry and platform permissions. Confirm API auth, loopback-only operation, OS credential storage, containment, per-tool consent and reproducible install/update policy.

### D. Measured proof-of-concept plan — separate approval required
Specify (do not execute) a **read-only** pilot: two end-to-end company reports, one ETF and/or savings-bank research case, one stale/conflicting-data case and one offline install/launch case. Compare existing local LLM plus Python workflow with Hermes on:
- numerical/source extraction correctness and evidence provenance; citations/relevant pages; point-in-time cutoff;
- abstention on unknown, stale or conflicting figures; no imaginary prices;
- latency, CPU/RAM/VRAM, token/API cost, startup/install size and failure/retry behaviour;
- no privileged tool use, no external writes, model-unavailable and shutdown fallback;
- incremental value versus built-in scheduler/provider adapters and existing scoring.

## Research-only deliverables / closure criteria

- [ ] Source-verified Windows distribution/API/runtime compatibility matrix, *observed versus documented* clearly distinguished.
- [ ] Security/privacy and third-party licence assessment with fail-closed tool-policy proposal.
- [ ] Read-only architecture schematic and threat model, plus complete installer/first-run/update/uninstall design.
- [ ] Specific restricted app tools and integrations, and pilot tasks, budgets, baseline metrics and acceptance/rejection thresholds.
- [ ] Decision: **adopt for bounded implementation / optional experiment / reject**, with open questions and evidence.
- [ ] If implementation is later authorised, request a new **canonical work item** through Codex root. No acceptance/implementation inference from closing this research ticket.

## Sources (revalidate before recommendation)

- [Hermes Agent official repository](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)
- [Programmatic integration: ACP, JSON-RPC, HTTP API](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/programmatic-integration)
- [HTTP API server](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/api-server)
- [Native Windows guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/windows-native)
- [Security](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/security)
- [MIT licence](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/LICENSE)
- [Existing related open research issue #999](https://github.com/Thor2709/etf_ai_cockpit/issues/999): PySpur, InsightSentry and FlexReport (avoid duplicating their scope)
- [App README](https://github.com/Thor2709/etf_ai_cockpit/blob/main/README.md) | [App rules](https://github.com/Thor2709/etf_ai_cockpit/blob/main/AGENTS.md)

**Evidence level:** upstream technical features/architecture documented; bundled ETF installer, real-world stock research accuracy and performance **not yet tested**. This is research, not an executable work authorisation.

## Phân tích sâu Hermes Agent

# Báo cáo Hermes Agent — 2026-10-25

## 📊 Tóm tắt hôm nay

Ngày bận rộn với 9 PR merged (chủ yếu bugfix), 30+ issue được cập nhật. Focus: sửa lỗi plugins bị tắt sau update, khôi phục Kanban desktop delivery, cải thiện update process trên Windows. Không có release mới.

---

## 🚀 Releases

Không có release trong 24h qua.

---

## 📈 Tiến độ dự án

### PRs merged quan trọng (9 PRs)

**Plugin ecosystem stability** (#144220)
- **Vấn đề**: Plugins có dependency không hỗ trợ Android (mnemosyne/onnxruntime, torch) bị tắt mỗi lần update trên Linux/macOS
- **Sửa**: Skip compatibility check nếu platform không chạy Android
- **Impact**: mnemosyne và torch-backed plugins không còn bị disable sai

**Web search toolset visibility** (#144215, #134617, #140643)
- **Vấn đề**: Sau Blank Slate setup, bật "web" toolset không load `web_search` (chỉ có `web_extract`)
- **Root cause**: Internal `search` toolset không register vào `CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS`, config disabled nó khi enable `web`
- **Sửa**: Surface `search` trong CLI picker, fix subset removal logic
- **Result**: `hermes tools` bật web → `web_search` hoạt động; `hermes tools list` cảnh báo disabled toolset ẩn tools

**Model download reliability** (#144211)
- Interrupted downloads resume từ bytes đã lưu (cả khi process bị kill)
- Connection drop nhiều lần vẫn thành công nếu còn tiến triển
- Salvage từ #143453 (@ocasta181)

**Gateway & Desktop fixes**
- #144231: Khôi phục Kanban delivery tới local Desktop sessions (wake events vào FIFO, toast notifications)
- #144180: `tool_search` catalog giữ descriptions cho small servers khi có huge MCP server; `hermes plugins install` interactive answer "y" load plugin vào gateway đang chạy
- #140594: Verify-on-stop không nudge 2 lần cho 1 edit; bash wrapper record exit status cho từng pipeline segment

**Prompt optimization** (#144173, #144216)
- `browser_exec` không còn nói với vision models "Your model cannot view images"
- 4 tool schemas drop 319 tokens/call (tools: 14,487 → 14,168)
- One-shot sessions giữ synchronous delegation; compression tail cap cover big windows

**Test stability** (#144224, #144229, #144230)
- Model picker không đợi 16s khi offline (chỉ lần đầu, sau đó skip 5 phút)
- Usage test và ACP editor-MCP fork test không còn flake under CI load
- #129837: NixOS `extraPythonPackages` không drop dependency groups

**Shell & config fixes**
- #144232: `_wrap_command_script` restore shell options sau wrapped command (leak `set -e` vào epilogue)
- #142528: Windows PM runtime lease files được prune (trước tích lũy 1,546 files)

### PRs đang review (11 PRs open)

**Feature: Tool execution safeguards**
- #141018: Bot Desktop screen tự stop sau idle window (discussion: abandoned screen lifecycle)
- #114586: Kanban completion safeguards (live-verification gate, liveness surfacing, stale-work watchdog)

**Bug fixes in review**
